Population increased in Cornwall

The estimated population of Cornwall in 2024 was 583,289 usual residents, a rise of 0.7% since 2023.

This meant that Cornwall's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Cornwall increased by 2%.

Over this slightly longer period, Cornwall was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Cornwall

The average (median) age stayed at 48 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Cornwall has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Cornwall is an area that is classed as rural in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Cornwall's population of 583,289 usual residents was made up of:

  • 92,891 people aged 0 to 15 years, (15.9%)
  • 338,792 people aged 16 to 64 years, (58.1%)
  • 151,606 people aged 65 years and over, (26%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Cornwall has a higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (26% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Cornwall, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net internal migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Cornwall
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Cornwall, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 2,592 people (-0.4%). In total, there were 4,241 births and 6,833 deaths in Cornwall.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 5,117 (0.9%). There were 25,065 people entering the area and 19,948 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Cornwall's population of 1,352 (0.2%) as a result of 3,186 people entering the area and 1,834 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Cornwall was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Cornwall in mid-2023 is 579,381.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 649 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 403 people.

In the 'other change' category (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners), we have revised the 2023 figure upwards by 5 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 1,057 people.
